title: Last character on longest line in script editor does not render when Display Scale is 125%
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.6-stable, 4.6-rc1,2, 4.6-dev1,2,3, 4.5.1-stable
- Not reproducible in: 4.1-stable

### System information

Godot v4.6.stable - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 3 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - AMD Radeon RX 5700 XT (Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.; 32.0.21037.1004) - AMD Ryzen 7 3700X 8-Core Processor (16 threads) - 31.92 GiB memory

### Issue description

With 4.6, it looks like Godot's Editor setting 'Display Scale', when set to Auto, will respect whatever Display Scale I have Windows set to (125%). Up until 4.6-dev3, with the introduction of the new theme, Auto would be 100%. After dev3, Auto would be 125%. Thus, I never noticed this bug until I updated to 4.6-stable (my first time on 4.6 moving from 4.5.1).

When Display Scale is set to 125%, the longest line in a file, long enough to warrant the appearance of the horizontal scroll bar, will not render the last character. The space of the character is there, it is selectable, it is modifiable, but it simply renders blank, like a space character. When Display Scale is set back to 100%, it renders normally. This bug persists regardless of my Windows Display Scale being set to 100% or 125%.

### Steps to reproduce

Set `Interface > Editor > Display Scale` to 125%.
Open any file in the editor (I've been testing on .gd script files). Simply fill a line with text until the horizontal bar appears, or if it already existed, until that line is the longest line in the file. Then add one more unique character and see that it will not render.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

N/A - happens on newly created projects
